group.title: Society and politics
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: A system where people choose their government by voting.
examples: In a {democracy}, citizens elect their leaders.
wrong: In a democracy, nobody is allowed to vote.

words.meaning: The group of elected people who make the laws of a country.
examples: The new law was passed by {parliament}.
wrong: Parliament is a kind of court for small crimes.

words.meaning: A member of the government in charge of an area.
wrong: A minister is a student in a primary school.

words.meaning: A plan of action agreed by a government or company.
wrong: A policy is a random choice made with no plan.

words.meaning: To show your choice in an election.
wrong: I voted by staying at home and doing nothing.

words.meaning: Planned actions to achieve a goal, like winning an election.
examples: She ran a strong {campaign} for mayor.
wrong: A campaign is one quick action with no plan.

words.meaning: The things everyone is allowed to have or do by law.
examples: Everyone has the {rights} to free speech and fair trials.
wrong: Rights are the things the law stops everyone from doing.

words.meaning: The act of coming to live in a new country.
examples: {Immigration} has made the city more diverse.
wrong: Immigration is leaving your country and never arriving anywhere.

words.meaning: The state of not having a job; the number of people without jobs.
wrong: Unemployment is the number of people who have jobs.

words.meaning: Help from the government for people who need it.
examples: The family lived on {welfare} for a year.
wrong: Welfare is a tax that poor people pay to the rich.

words.meaning: An unfair situation where some people have more than others.
examples: There is great {inequality} between rich and poor.
wrong: Inequality means everyone has exactly the same.

words.meaning: Treating people unfairly because of who they are.
wrong: Discrimination means treating everyone in exactly the same fair way.

words.meaning: A change made to improve a system.
wrong: A reform is a change that keeps everything the same.

words.meaning: Dishonest behavior by people in power, often for money.
wrong: Corruption is the honest work of a good leader.

words.meaning: An event that shocks people because it is wrong.
examples: The {scandal} forced the minister to resign.
wrong: A scandal is a quiet event that nobody cares about.

words.meaning: More than half of a group.
wrong: The majority is the smallest part of the group.

words.meaning: Less than half of a group.
wrong: The minority is more than half of all people.

words.meaning: The parties in parliament that are not in government.
wrong: The opposition is the party that runs the government.

words.meaning: Laws, or the process of making laws.
wrong: Legislation is a kind of election poster.

words.meaning: The people who live in one area or share something.
examples: The whole {community} helped after the flood.
wrong: A community is one person who lives alone.

words.meaning: A range of different people or things.
examples: The school is proud of its cultural {diversity}.
wrong: Diversity means everyone is exactly the same.

words.meaning: A building where criminals are kept.
wrong: A prison is a hotel where people go on holiday.

words.meaning: Something done to a person because they did wrong.
examples: The {punishment} for stealing was a large fine.
wrong: A punishment is a prize for good behavior.

words.meaning: A person who is harmed by a crime or accident.
examples: The {victim} of the robbery called the police.
wrong: The victim is the person who committed the crime.

words.meaning: A person who the police think may have done a crime.
wrong: A suspect is a person who is certainly innocent and not involved.

words.meaning: The process in court to decide if someone is guilty.
wrong: A trial is a party after a court case.

words.meaning: The punishment a court gives.
wrong: A sentence is a reward the judge gives to the victim.

words.meaning: For everyone, or connected with the government.
examples: This is a {public} park; anyone can come in.
wrong: It’s a public beach, so only the owner can use it.

words.meaning: For one person or group only.
examples: This is a {private} road; no entry.
wrong: It’s a private room, so everyone can come in.

words.meaning: To choose someone for a job by voting.
wrong: We elected him without anyone voting.

words.meaning: To officially say that something is not allowed.
examples: The city {banned} cars from the center.
wrong: They banned smoking, so everyone can smoke.

words.meaning: To discuss a subject formally with different opinions.
examples: Parliament {debated} the new law for hours.
wrong: They debated the law without saying a word.

words.meaning: To try to persuade politicians to support something.
examples: Farmers {lobbied} the government for more help.
wrong: They lobbied the minister by never talking to anyone.

words.meaning: Affecting the whole world.
wrong: It’s a global problem, so it only affects one village.

words.meaning: Connected with society and the way people live together.
wrong: Poverty is a social problem, so it has nothing to do with society.

words.meaning: Having no home.
wrong: He is homeless, so he owns three houses.

words.meaning: A person who has to leave their country because of war or danger.
wrong: A refugee is a tourist on a holiday.

words.meaning: An official count of a country’s population.
examples: The {census} showed the city had grown.
wrong: A census is a guess with no counting.

words.meaning: A time of great danger or difficulty.
examples: The country is in an economic {crisis}.
wrong: A crisis is a calm period with no problems.

words.meaning: A person who takes part in a protest.
wrong: A protester is a person who agrees with everything quietly.
